chapter: Russell's band, records and Armstrong in the studio
title: The Savoy beat and Russell's band winning band battles
summary: Only young people could dance to swing; the right beat won applause and Russell's band, in and out of the Savoy like a house band, beat all rivals.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: You had to be young for that.

Oh yeah. Only young people could do it. The old ones do it and break their neck. All the young ones couldn't do it -- because I didn't want to do it. Yeah, it was strictly young people's music. That swinging music, that's strictly for young folks. At the Savoy you had that bright beat. You didn't have nothin' to worry about in the (?). Because if you have the right, by the time you finish your number, boy, that applause is going to bring you back again. But if you don't have the right beat when you finish your number, you just go into your next number. And when you sometimes get off the stand, they let you just get off the stand. The other band take over. But if you got the right beat on them now, in your last number, you don't get off the stand. They're not going to let you off. The applause is going to keep you right up there. And then all the bands started to do the best they could up there, get as

much applause as they could get.
That's why I worked in the Savoy so many different times. Russell's band was in and out of the Savoy just like he was the house band in there. So many, you know, different times... Because they knew the beat, what the dancers wanted. Like when we would have a battle of music there, nobody outshone Luis Russell's band. Because when he got through certain numbers...well, I mean, that was all she wrote.
